key_insight: The paper shows that retrieval can help models learn reasoning by analogy, not just by surface similarity. By pairing retrieval with reinforcement-based post-training, the model can discover and reuse reasoning patterns that transfer across seemingly different problems.
problem_solved: Standard RAG retrieves examples or documents that look semantically similar, but that often fails on reasoning tasks where the best helper problem may look different on the surface while sharing the same solution pattern. This paper addresses the gap between retrieval based on similarity and retrieval based on reasoning structure.
method: Introduces Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RA-RFT), a post-training framework that combines retrieval with reinforcement learning.
Uses retrieved examples to guide the model toward analogous reasoning strategies rather than only matching topical or lexical similarity.
Optimizes the model to reinforce retrieval choices and reasoning paths that improve task performance on complex problems.
impact: This approach could make AI systems better at solving hard multi-step tasks by learning which prior examples are truly useful for reasoning transfer. For practitioners, it offers a path to more reliable RAG systems on tasks where naive similarity search is not enough.

paper_title: Learning to Reason by Analogy via Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
paper_authors: Zilin Xiao, Qi Ma, Chun-cheng Jason Chen, Xintao Chen, Avinash Atreya
